method: Specific energy is energy divided by mass, a coherent SI derived quantity whose unit is the joule per kilogram (J/kg); it is not energy density, which is energy per volume in J/m3 and needs the density as well. The page converts every unit through joules per kilogram from exact factors. A kilowatt hour is 3,600,000 J, so 1 kWh/kg is 3.6 MJ/kg and 1 Wh/kg is 3,600 J/kg; a megajoule per kilogram is a gigajoule per tonne because a tonne is 1,000 kg; a gram is a thousandth of a kilogram, so 1 cal/g is 1,000 cal per kg, which is why cal/g and kcal/kg are the same size; and 1 Btu/lb is 1055.05585262 J divided by 0.45359237 kg, exactly 2326 J/kg. The calorie is the thermochemical calorie of 4.184 J, the one used for food energy, and the BTU is the International Table BTU, not the thermochemical one, so a value copied from a table built on the other definition differs in the fourth significant digit. The chosen pair is the headline result and all nine units are listed in three groups, so the SI, fuel and imperial readings stay visible together. An optional mass in kilograms multiplies the specific energy by that mass and reports the total energy in megajoules and kilowatt hours, which is the step from a fuel's energy content to the energy in a tank or a batch. Results are rounded to six significant digits and grouped in thousands; values below 0.0001 or at least 1e13 are printed in exponent form so that 1 J/kg does not collapse to zero in MJ/kg. Input is a plain decimal number, optionally grouped with commas, from zero up to 1,000 MJ/kg (1 GJ/kg) and a mass from zero up to 1,000 tonnes; exponent notation, text, a misplaced comma and negative values are refused with a specific message rather than clipped. This is unit arithmetic only: lower and higher heating values differ for every fuel, a cell's usable energy is below its cell-level specific energy, and no combustion, efficiency, temperature or density model is applied. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 811, Guide for the Use of the International System of Units (SI), 2008 edition: Table 4 gives specific energy as a coherent derived quantity in joule per kilogram (J/kg)
NIST Special Publication 811, 2008 edition, Appendix B conversion factors: British thermal unit (IT) 1055.05585262 J, thermochemical calorie 4.184 J and avoirdupois pound 0.45359237 kg
